description: PM-7b plan browser. No fixture: it clears user://ai_plans/, writes exactly one plan there from the shipped test fixture, and opens the browser from the menu with a real click. Asserts the row carries name / army / zone / terrain / validation badge / source, that selecting it fills the detail line and enables the user-plan actions, that Rename moves both the row and the file (and rewrites the plan's own name), that Delete goes through a confirmation step and only removes the file once confirmed, and that closing the browser refreshes the seat pickers so a deleted plan cannot still be chosen. Nothing ships under res://data/ai_plans yet, so the read-only half is asserted against PlanManager directly: rename_plan and delete_plan both refuse a res:// path and the file survives.

steps.script:
# Rows are found BY NAME, not by index. This scenario used to assume the
# browser contained exactly one plan — the fixture it writes — which stopped
# being true the moment PM-10 shipped plans in res://data/ai_plans/. The
# browser was right and the test was wrong. What this scenario is actually
# about is the lifecycle of the user's OWN plan, so it now counts and locates
# user rows and is indifferent to how much content ships alongside them.
var d = node.get_node("/root/MainMenu/PlanBrowserDialog")
var t = node.get_node("/root/MainMenu/PlanBrowserDialog/PlanBrowserRoot/PlanBrowserTree")
var mine = 0
var total = 0
var item = t.get_root().get_first_child()
while item != null:
	total += 1
	if item.get_text(5) == "yours":
		mine += 1
	item = item.get_next()
print("SCENARIO pm7b browser rows: %d total, %d yours (the rest are shipped)" % [total, mine])
return "mine=%d total>=%d" % [mine, 1 if total >= 1 else 0]

# Rows are found BY NAME, not by index. This scenario used to assume the
# browser contained exactly one plan — the fixture it writes — which stopped
# being true the moment PM-10 shipped plans in res://data/ai_plans/. The
# browser was right and the test was wrong. What this scenario is actually
# about is the lifecycle of the user's OWN plan, so it now counts and locates
# user rows and is indifferent to how much content ships alongside them.
var txt = node.get_node("/root/MainMenu/PlanBrowserDialog").status_label.text
print("SCENARIO pm7b status line: %s" % txt)
return txt.ends_with("1 of your own.")
